sections.content: How many people are "bank and post office clerks"?

76,755 people

were counted on the census as "bank and post office clerks" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Bank and post office clerks deal with the payment and receipt of money, cheques and other routine financial transactions and open and close accounts.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "bank and post office clerks" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "bank and post office clerks", 12.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "bank and post office clerks" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "bank and post office clerks" included:

  • science, engineering and production technicians (other)
  • assemblers and routine operatives (other)
  • records clerks and assistants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "bank and post office clerks" there were more women than men (70.3% compared with 29.7%).

This means "bank and post office clerks" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 29.7% and women made up 70.3% of "bank and post office clerks"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "bank and post office clerks" included:

  • dispensing opticians
  • housing officers
  • coffee shop workers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "bank and post office clerks" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "bank and post office clerks" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "bank and post office clerks", 10.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (59.6% compared with 40.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.2%) than self-employed (4.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
